rationale: I read the complete held EO 9593 (10 FR 9379, July 28, 1945, signed July 25, 1945): it authorizes and directs the Secretary of War to take possession of and operate the plants and facilities of the Springfield Plywood Corporation, Springfield, Oregon, under the War Labor Disputes Act (paras. 1-5). Para. 5 is its own end mechanism: possession is to be terminated by the Secretary of War within 60 days after he determines that prior productive efficiency has been restored; no such determination is held, so para. 5 gives no date and I do not rely on it as the basis. I read the held text of EO 9603 (Aug. 25, 1945, 'Termination of Possession of Certain Property Taken by the Government'): all plants, mines, facilities and other property seized or taken 'under and pursuant to the following-described Executive orders, or amendments thereof, shall be returned to the owners thereof as soon as practicable', and the list includes 'No. 9593 of July 25, 1945'; any listed order in conflict is amended to the extent of conflict. The sole operative effect of EO 9593 is the seizure and operation of that one company's plants, so a direction to return all property taken under it exhausts every part of the order; there is no savings clause, no partial list, and no remaining continuing function. The order does not use the word revoked, and 'as soon as practicable' fixes no first-end date, so this is a functional end by a later instrument that names the order, which I record as a hypothesis, not an adjudicated first end. D6 self-check: the only history lead is the OFR cross-reference 'See: EO 9603, August 25, 1945', which the text bears out; the 1989 snapshot row is empty. No later held instrument mentions EO 9593, there is no amendment, extension or re-seizure, and EO 9603 contains no exception for EO 9593. The statutory basis (War Labor Disputes Act) was not examined.
